Class Exercise 1. Since bind_cols() just combines two data frames by putting them side-by-side, the observations must be in the same order in each of the two data frames.

Class Exercise 2.

```{r}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
slumajors_df <- read_csv(here("data/SLU_Majors_17_21.csv"))
collegemajors_df <- read_csv(here("data/college-majors.csv"))
glimpse(slumajors_df)
glimpse(collegemajors_df)

left_join(slumajors_df, collegemajors_df, join_by(Major == Major))
## keys must match exactly for the join to work
## (here, they don't match because they are in title case in one
## data set and all caps in the other)
```

Class Exercise 3.

```{r}
imdb_episodes <- read_csv(here::here("data/imdb_episodes.csv"))
imdb_info <- read_csv(here::here("data/imdb_info.csv"))
imdb_showrating <- read_csv(here::here("data/imdb_showrating.csv"))
```

The key is a unique identification number for the television show: `show_id` in `imdb_episodes` and `parentTconst` in the other two data sets.

Class Exercises 4 through 8

Class Exercise 4.

```{r}
show_info <- bind_cols(imdb_info, imdb_showrating)
## see class exercise 1.
## safer option would be to use a join with the parentTconst key
```

Class Exercise 5.

```{r}
left_join(imdb_episodes, show_info, join_by(show_id == parentTconst...1))
```

Dropping any tv show that is in show_info that does not have episode ratings in imdb_episodes.

Class Exercise 6.

```{r}
left_join(show_info, imdb_episodes, join_by(parentTconst...1 == show_id))

```

any shows that do not appear in show info but that have episode ratings in the imdb_epiodes.

Class Exercise 7.

```{r}
imdb_ep10 <- imdb_episodes |> group_by(show_id) |>
  summarise(n = n()) |>
  filter(n > 10)

semi_join(show_info, imdb_ep10, join_by(parentTconst...1 == show_id))
```

Class Exercise 8.

```{r}
imdb_episodes
show_pop <- show_info |> filter(averageRating >= 8 & numVotes >= 200000)
semi_join(imdb_episodes, show_pop, join_by(show_id == parentTconst...1))
```
